propositions.statement: p is an arbitrary prime, K is an arbitrary field with Char K=p, and λ is an integer with 0≤λ<p.

V is the complex irreducible highest-weight sl₂(C)-module of highest weight λ and complex dimension λ+1. Its endomorphisms x,y,h satisfy hx−xh=2x, hy−yh=−2y and xy−yx=h. The vector v∈V is nonzero and satisfies xv=0 and hv=λv.

M⊂V is an arbitrary free abelian subgroup with an integer basis which is also a complex basis of V, and M is stable under the integer enveloping subalgebra generated by all X_r=x^r/r! and Y_r=y^r/r! (r∈N). The induced x,y,h actions on V(K)=M⊗_Z K are the actions in the target.

For i=0,…,λ, the vectors e_i=y^iv/i! form a complex basis of V. They satisfy xe_0=0, xe_i=(λ−i+1)e_(i−1) for 1≤i≤λ, ye_i=(i+1)e_(i+1) for i<λ, ye_λ=0, and he_i=(λ−2i)e_i. For every r≥0, X_r e_i=binom(λ−i+r,r)e_(i−r) if r≤i and zero otherwise; Y_r e_i=binom(i+r,r)e_(i+r) if i+r≤λ and zero otherwise.

For i,j∈{0,…,λ}, let E_ij be the complex linear map sending e_j to e_i and every e_k with k≠j to zero, and put c_j=binom(λ,j), A_ij=X_(λ−i)Y_λX_λY_(λ−j), and D=∏_(t=0)^λ c_t. Each A_ij preserves M, A_ij=c_jE_ij, A_ij A_kl=δ_(jk)c_j A_il, and D Id_V=Σ_(i=0)^λ(∏_(t≠i)c_t)A_ii.
For every j with 0≤j≤λ the integer c_j=binom(λ,j) has nonzero image in K; for every r with 0≤r≤λ the integer r! has nonzero image in K. Hence D=∏_(j=0)^λ c_j also has nonzero image in K.

Let A_ij^K denote the operator induced by A_ij|_M on U=M⊗_Z K and define F_ij=(c_j in K)^(-1) A_ij^K for 0≤i,j≤λ. Then F_ij F_kl=δ_(jk)F_il and Σ_(i=0)^λ F_ii=Id_U. For 0≤r≤λ the induced divided powers satisfy (r! in K)X_r^K=(x^K)^r and (r! in K)Y_r^K=(y^K)^r.
The K-vector space U=M⊗_Z K has dimension λ+1, and U≠0.
Every K-linear subspace W⊂U=M⊗_Z K invariant under the induced x,y,h operators is invariant under every F_ij=(binom(λ,j) in K)^(-1)(X_(λ−i)Y_λX_λY_(λ−j))^K for 0≤i,j≤λ.

The vector space V(K)=M⊗_Z K is nonzero, and every K-linear subspace invariant under the induced x,y,h is either zero or all of V(K), for all the original parameters including λ=0, p=2, and arbitrary fields K of characteristic p.
Let K be a field, U a finite-dimensional K-vector space, ι a finite type, and v:ι→U a linearly independent family. If card ι=dim_K U, then span_K(range v)=U.
Let K be any field, M any Z-module, and b a Z-basis of M indexed by an arbitrary type ι. There exists a K-basis B of K⊗_Z M indexed by the same ι with B_i=1⊗b_i.

Let K be any field and M any Z-module. There is a unital ring homomorphism ρ:End_Z(M)→End_K(K⊗_Z M) such that ρ(t)(a⊗m)=a⊗t(m) for every t,a,m. It preserves integer multiples as every unital ring homomorphism does, as well as sums, compositions, identity and powers.
For a prime p, a ring A with CharP A p, and n∈N, the element n! cast to A is a unit if and only if n<p.
For natural numbers n,k with k≤n, choose(n,k)·k!·(n−k)!=n!.
For any field K, K-vector space U, arbitrary index type ι, and basis b:Basis ι K U, dim_K U (the natural finrank) equals Nat.card ι.
For any field K and Z-module M there is an additive equivalence e:M⊗_Z K≃K⊗_Z M satisfying e(m⊗a)=a⊗m. Additivity makes e and its inverse Z-linear automatically.

Let K be any field, U a finite-dimensional K-vector space and n∈N with dim_K U=n. Suppose F_ij∈End_K(U), indexed by i,j∈Fin n, satisfy F_ij F_kl=(if j=k then F_il else 0) and Σ_i F_ii=Id. Every K-subspace W invariant under all F_ij is zero or U. No positivity hypothesis on n is needed for this dichotomy.
